lecture_16.title: CS336 Spring 2026, Lecture 16: Post-training 2, reinforcement learning from verifiable rewards
lecture_16.anchor_convention: lecture_16.pdf:p<page>, page numbers from `pdftotext -layout` form feeds (title slide = p1; p62 is an empty trailing page)
lecture_16.note: Evidence is the text layer of the slides (lecture_16.txt), extracted page-by-page by discover_slides.py (sha256 of txt in discovered.json). The deck is screenshot-heavy: the PPO objective (p7), the AlpacaFarm loss/rollout code (p11-p13), the GAE formula (p15), the GRPO objective and the nano-aha-moment advantage code (p18-p20), the Dr. GRPO objective (p23), every results table/plot (p21, p29-p30, p36, p47-p48, p53-p54) and the Kimi RL setup (p46) are images; only their captions survive in the text layer. Numbers visible only in those images are recorded in filtering_note, never in statements or prompts.

lecture_16_video.title: CS336 Spring 2026, Lecture 16: Post-training 2, reinforcement learning from verifiable rewards (lecture video)

lecture_15.title: CS336 Spring 2026, Lecture 15: Post-training 1 (SFT, RLHF, DPO)
lecture_15.note: Prerequisite deck: reward models, RLHF, DPO and the overoptimization warning (p62-p63 of lecture_15.pdf). No atlas thread exists for it yet, so external_prerequisites of the form lecture_15:<topic> are placeholders (basis author-inference) and no quotes are anchored into it.

feynrl_repo.title: FeynRL: RL post-training library (local clone; atlas thread atlas/repos/feynrl)
feynrl_repo.note: The repo thread implements the mechanisms these slides describe: feynrl:grpo-clipped-loss (ratio = exp(logp - old_logp), min/clip), feynrl:group-relative-advantage (z-score within a prompt's n_samples), feynrl:kl-reference-penalty (reference model loaded only if kl_coeff > 0), feynrl:supp-importance-ratio, feynrl:cispo-vs-ppo-clip, feynrl:sync-epoch-loop and feynrl:staleness-budget-max-lag. Referenced through external_prerequisites and see_also (ids are feynrl:<kp-id>); no line anchors are placed from this thread.

ppo_paper.title: Proximal Policy Optimization Algorithms (Schulman, Wolski, Dhariwal, Radford, Klimov, 2017)
ppo_paper.note: Slide p6 shows the 2017 PPO announcement blog and OpenAI Five (2019); p5 names TRPO (Schulman et al. 2015, arXiv:1502.05477) as 'Attempt 2'.

spinningup_ppo.title: OpenAI Spinning Up: Proximal Policy Optimization
spinningup_ppo.note: Slide p7 reproduces the PPO-Clip objective figure from this page; the objective itself is image-only in the deck.

alpaca_farm_ppo.title: AlpacaFarm PPO trainer (tatsu-lab/alpaca_farm, src/alpaca_farm/rl/ppo_trainer.py @30717dd)
alpaca_farm_ppo.note: Slides p10-p16 walk through this implementation (outer loop, loss with Cliprange=0.2, rollouts, per-token KL reward shaping, GAE). Code is shown as screenshots.

zheng_2023_secrets_rlhf.title: Secrets of RLHF in Large Language Models Part I: PPO (Zheng et al., 2023)
zheng_2023_secrets_rlhf.note: Slide p9 ('From Zheng et al 2023'): the token-level MDP picture for PPO on language models.

deepseekmath_grpo.title: DeepSeekMath: Pushing the Limits of Mathematical Reasoning in Open Language Models (Shao et al., 2024)
deepseekmath_grpo.note: Origin of GRPO. Slide p18 shows its PPO-vs-GRPO figure; p21 its results against RFT with and without process supervision; p27 and p38 cite it for R1's choice of GRPO and for the PRM negative results.

nano_aha_moment.title: nano-aha-moment: a single-file GRPO implementation (McGill-NLP)
nano_aha_moment.note: Slides p19-p20 walk through its reward, per-group mean/var normalization (with a 1e-4 stability term in the std), KL term and gradient update.

sutton_barto.title: Reinforcement Learning: An Introduction (Sutton and Barto, 2nd ed., 2018)
sutton_barto.note: Slide p22 shows the baseline-subtraction passage: any state-dependent term may be subtracted from the reward without biasing the policy gradient.

dr_grpo.title: Understanding R1-Zero-Like Training: A Critical Perspective (Dr. GRPO; Liu et al., 2025)
dr_grpo.note: Slide p23 ('Liu et al 2025') shows the unbiased GRPO objective (drops the std division and the per-response length normalizer); p24 the length-bias analysis; p30 the follow-up analyses that the R1-Zero length growth is partly due to the biased objective and that the base model already shows 'aha' behaviour.

deepseek_r1.title: DeepSeek-R1: Incentivizing Reasoning Capability in LLMs via Reinforcement Learning (DeepSeek-AI, 2025)
deepseek_r1.note: Case study p26-p38: R1-Zero (accuracy + format rewards on DeepSeek-V3 base), R1 (reasoning SFT, GRPO with language-consistency reward, SFT/RLHF), distillation into Qwen 2.5, and the unsuccessful-attempts section (PRMs, MCTS).

s1_simple_test_time_scaling.title: s1: Simple test-time scaling (Muennighoff et al., 2025)
s1_simple_test_time_scaling.note: Inferred source of slide p33 ('1k Math and science questions + Long CoTs from Gemini / r1'); the slide does not name the paper (basis: inference).

prm800k_lets_verify.title: Let's Verify Step by Step (Lightman et al., 2023; PRM800K)
prm800k_lets_verify.note: Slide p38 names PRM800k alongside DeepSeekMath under 'unsuccessful attempts' (process reward models).

kimi_k15.title: Kimi k1.5: Scaling Reinforcement Learning with LLMs (Kimi Team, 2025)
kimi_k15.note: Case study p39-p48: difficulty filtering (fail on best-of-8, no multiple choice), long-CoT SFT, DPO-derived squared-loss policy gradient, length reward with lambda in [0.5, -0.5], curriculum by (1 - success_rate), RL infra, scaling results and the expert-iteration ablation.

qwen3_report.title: Qwen3 Technical Report (Qwen Team, 2025)
qwen3_report.note: Case study p49-p54: difficulty filtering by best-of-n, GRPO on only 3995 examples, thinking-mode fusion, test-time scaling, and the stage-composition table where math/STEM drops slightly after general RLHF.

qwen3_coder_next.title: Qwen3-Coder-Next (Qwen Team, 2026)
qwen3_coder_next.note: Slides p55-p60 (agentic RL, mid-training sources, expert models, 800k SWE-bench-style environments). Frontier material; not made into KPs, recorded in rl-infra-cost's filtering_note.
